title: Opposite-side castling: the race
summary: When kings castle on opposite wings, speed decides: pawn storms, open files, and material matters less than tempo.

steps.md:
With kings on opposite wings, both sides can **storm with pawns** without weakening their own king. The game becomes a race:

- **Tempo is everything:** count how many moves each attack needs to open a file against the king.
- Use **pawns to open files** (g4-g5, h4-h5 against a kingside king; ...b5-b4, ...a5-a4 against a queenside king). Sacrificing a pawn or the exchange to open a file is normal (Dragon ...Rxc3).
- **Defensive moves only when forced**; a move that slows the opponent by one tempo can be worth as much as an attacking move.
- Avoid opening files against your own king (do not capture towards your own king if it opens a line for him).

Yugoslav Attack against the Dragon. White has castled long and plays h4-h5 and g4 to open the h-file; Black has castled short and plays ...Rc8, ...Ne5-c4 and the exchange sacrifice ...Rxc3 against the queenside king.

steps.question: In an opposite-castling race, your opponent offers a pawn on the wing where your king lives. Accepting would open a file towards your own king. Usually you should...
choices: Decline and keep attacking: tempo and closed files near your king matter more than a pawn
steps.explain: In races the currency is time and open lines. Taking a pawn that opens a file towards your king often loses the race.

steps.question: Which pawn advance usually opens lines fastest against a king on g8 with pawns f7, g7, h7 (or after ...h5)?
choices: g4-g5 or h4-h5 levers that attack the pawn cover directly
steps.explain: Levers against the pawn shield (h4-h5 against ...g6, g4 against ...h5) force files open. Pawns on the other wing do nothing for the attack.

steps.prompt: White to move. The black king on c8 has lost its pawn cover. Strike first.
steps.explain: **32.Qb7+! Kd8 33.Nxe6+** forks the king and the f4-queen. The exposed king on the queenside allowed the queen to check from b7 and the knight to join with tempo.

steps.prompt: White to move. Black has just played ...Rxd4, attacking your queen. Your a-pawn has reached a5 next to the black king.
steps.explain: **24.axb6!** ignores the attack on the queen and opens the black king. After 24...Rxe4 25.bxc7+ Kxc7 26.Nxe4 White comes out ahead in material with the black king exposed. Pawn levers against the castled king are worth more than a queen when they come with tempo.

steps.question: Typical error in opposite-castling positions:
choices: Making a "safe" prophylactic move when the race requires every tempo for the attack
Pushing pawns towards the enemy king
Opening a file with a sacrifice
steps.explain: The side that hesitates usually loses the race. Prophylaxis is right only when it costs the opponent more time than it costs you.

steps.md: **Retrieval check.** What decides opposite-castling races? (Tempo and open files.) Which pawns do you push? (Those on the wing of the enemy king.) What do you avoid? (Opening files towards your own king.)

sources: Vukovic, The Art of Attack in Chess (1965)
Yugoslav Attack vs the Dragon, standard Sicilian theory
